title: The rest of Avot
hookLine: year one read chapters one and two; now the rest, saying by saying
tomorrow: Akavia says look at three things and you won't sin. which three?

cards: Somewhere there's a show you stopped in season two, still waiting under continue watching. Year one of this path did that with a book.

Pirkei Avot, the sayings of the fathers: the chain from Sinai, Hillel's if not now, when, Shammai's say little and do much, a skull floating on the water. Then chapter two ended, and the path moved on.
So what's in the rest? Four more chapters, and this season reads them, one saying at a time.

teach.b: A quick walk down the hall, no spoilers past the doors. Each saying is a sentence or two: small enough to carry in a pocket, hard enough to argue over for a week.
Chapter three opens with a sage named Akavia and three things to look at. Further on, Rabbi Akiva says every human being is beloved, because each was created in God's image.
Before he speaks of any one people, he speaks of everyone.
Chapter four has Ben Zoma's riddles. Who is rich? The one who is happy with their portion.

teach.h: CHAPTER FIVE: TURN IT, AND TURN IT.
teach.b: Chapter five counts things in tens and sevens and fours, and keeps the arguments that last because they were for heaven's sake. And Ben Bag Bag says of the Torah: turn it, and turn it again, for everything is in it.
Some sayings are gentle, some are hard, and a few will sound strange until a whole lesson opens them up.
Now the review round, because the rest of Avot lands on what you already carry. You read a verse alone: bereshit bara. You said thanks in the root of Judah's name: todah.
Letters count, and names matter. Judaism thinks and lives. And yesterday: read, then live.
Avot is where those meet: short sayings, each one something to do.

how: In Jewish custom Pirkei Avot is read on Shabbat afternoons in the summer months, a chapter a week, and it is printed in many prayer books; some read it with a study partner, saying by saying.

games.q: what does “the rest of avot” mean?
o: the closing books of the Hebrew Bible
the rabbis' notes in the margins of the Talmud
chapters three to six of the sages' sayings

games.q: the rest of Avot — who said it? tap the pairs.
p: turn it, and turn it again

s: Pirkei Avot ends after chapter two
year one stopped there. the book goes on, through chapter six.
in Avot, Rabbi Akiva calls every human being beloved
beloved is each person, created in God's image; he says it before he speaks of any one people.

games.q: a new kid joins your group project and seems to know less than everyone else. Ben Zoma has a riddle: who is wise?
o: the one who learns from every person, the new kid too.
the one in the group who already knows the most.
the one who works alone so no one slows them down.
games.why: in chapter four Ben Zoma answers his own riddle: wise is the one who learns from every person.

practice: Here is how chapter three begins, in plain words: Akavia ben Mahalalel says, look at three things, and you won't come into the hands of sin.

Say it once out loud, slowly, the way you'd read a line to a study partner across the table. Don't explain it yet; the three things are tomorrow's. For the rest of the sit, wonder which three you would have picked.
